children: Apple Inc. (AAPL, Financials), the consumer technology giant that makes the iPhone, was higher as investors examined its latest devices and increasing usage of artificial intelligence. Shares were up more than 1 percent in pre-market trade. That may not be much, but the time counts.
For much of the AI boom, Apple has felt the pressure to prove it isn't lagging behind its competition. This week's product launch gives investors something a little more tangible to appraise.

The business announced its new iPhone portfolio, including the iPhone Duo, and pushed AI further into its products. New Apple Watch features also revealed the company's intention to integrate A.I. into devices that people currently use every day.
That's where Apple has the edge. It doesn't have to convince millions of people to explore a new platform. The users are on the premises.
It remains to be seen whether those features are enough to get customers to buy a new gadget sooner than they otherwise would have. That's what will matter most to investors.

A better upgrade cycle might boost iPhone sales and take more customers further into Apple's services ecosystem. But even if demand remains soft, the firm will still have to answer questions about whether it's moving too slowly on AI.
The next indicator for investors will be early demand for the new iPhones. That will tell if AI is becoming a real sales engine or just another expected feature.

title: Apple Just Made Its Biggest iPhone Move in Years
